f: What does التصريف mean linguistically?
b: It means change or alteration (التغيير).

f: What does التصريف mean technically in Arabic morphology?
b: It is transforming one original form into different forms for intended meanings that cannot be obtained except through those forms.

f: Into what two categories is the verb divided according to the number of its original letters?
b: It is either trilateral (ثلاثي) or quadrilateral (رباعي).

f: What two categories apply to both triliteral and quadrilateral verbs?
b: Each is either basic/unaugmented (مجرد) or augmented (مزيد فيه).

f: What further division applies to both basic and augmented verbs?
b: Each is either sound (سالم) or unsound/non-sound (غير سالم).

f: What is meant by a sound verb (السالم) according to the morphologists?
b: It is a verb whose original letters, represented by ف، ع، ل, are free from weak letters, hamzah, and consonant doubling.

f: What are the three possible vowel patterns of the past tense of the basic triliteral verb?
b: The past tense may be فَعَلَ, فَعِلَ, or فَعُلَ, according to the vowel of the middle radical.

f: If the past tense of a basic triliteral verb is on the pattern فَعَلَ with a fatḥah on the middle radical, what are the possible patterns of its present tense?
b: Its present tense is either يَفْعُلُ with ḍammah on the middle radical or يَفْعِلُ with kasrah on the middle radical.

f: What are examples of a basic triliteral verb whose past is فَعَلَ and present is يَفْعُلُ?
b: نَصَرَ يَنْصُرُ.

f: What are examples of a basic triliteral verb whose past is فَعَلَ and present is يَفْعِلُ?
b: ضَرَبَ يَضْرِبُ.

f: When does a basic triliteral verb whose past is فَعَلَ take the present pattern يَفْعَلُ?
b: When either the middle radical (عين الفعل) or final radical (لام الفعل) is one of the six guttural letters.

f: What are the six guttural letters that cause a فَعَلَ verb to come on يَفْعَلُ?
b: ء، هـ، ع، ح، غ، خ.

f: What is an example of a verb whose middle radical is a guttural letter and whose present is on يَفْعَلُ?
b: سَأَلَ يَسْأَلُ.

f: What is an example of a verb whose final radical is a guttural letter and whose present is on يَفْعَلُ?
b: مَنَعَ يَمْنَعُ.

f: What is the ruling of أَبَى يَأْبَى with respect to this pattern?
b: It is anomalous (شاذّ).

f: If the past tense of a basic triliteral verb is on فَعِلَ with kasrah on the middle radical, what is the normal present-tense pattern?
b: يَفْعَلُ, with fatḥah on the middle radical.

f: What is an example of the فَعِلَ → يَفْعَلُ pattern?
b: عَلِمَ يَعْلَمُ.

f: Are there exceptions to the فَعِلَ → يَفْعَلُ pattern?
b: Yes. Some verbs are anomalous, such as حَسِبَ يَحْسِبُ and its counterparts.

f: If the past tense of a basic triliteral verb is on فَعُلَ with ḍammah on the middle radical, what is its present-tense pattern?
b: يَفْعُلُ, with ḍammah on the middle radical.

f: What is an example of the فَعُلَ → يَفْعُلُ pattern?
b: حَسُنَ يَحْسُنُ.

f: How many patterns does the basic quadrilateral verb have?
b: It has one pattern: فَعْلَلَ.

f: What is the basic quadrilateral verb pattern?
b: فَعْلَلَ.

f: Give an example of a basic quadrilateral verb together with its present tense and verbal noun.
b: دَحْرَجَ يُدَحْرِجُ دَحْرَجَةً، ودِحْراجًا.

f: Into how many categories is the augmented triliteral verb divided according to the number of letters in its past tense?
b: Into three categories: four-letter, five-letter, and six-letter past-tense forms.

f: What are the three categories of augmented triliteral verbs?
b: Four-letter forms, five-letter forms, and six-letter forms in the past tense.

f: What are the three four-letter augmented triliteral patterns mentioned?
b: أَفْعَلَ، فَعَّلَ، فَاعَلَ.

f: What is an example of the أَفْعَلَ pattern?
b: أَكْرَمَ يُكْرِمُ إِكْرَامًا.

f: What is an example of the فَعَّلَ pattern?
b: فَرَّحَ يُفَرِّحُ تَفْرِيحًا.

f: What is an example of the فَاعَلَ pattern?
b: قَاتَلَ يُقَاتِلُ مُقَاتَلَةً، وقِتَالًا، وقِيتَالًا.

f: What are the five-letter augmented triliteral patterns mentioned when the past tense begins with تاء?
b: تَفَعَّلَ and تَفَاعَلَ.

f: What is an example of the تَفَعَّلَ pattern?
b: تَكَسَّرَ يَتَكَسَّرُ تَكَسُّرًا.

f: What is an example of the تَفَاعَلَ pattern?
b: تَبَاعَدَ يَتَبَاعَدُ تَبَاعُدًا.

f: What are the five-letter augmented triliteral patterns mentioned that begin with همزة الوصل?
b: انْفَعَلَ، افْتَعَلَ، افْعَلَّ.

f: What is an example of the انْفَعَلَ pattern?
b: انْقَطَعَ يَنْقَطِعُ انْقِطَاعًا.

f: What is an example of the افْتَعَلَ pattern?
b: اجْتَمَعَ يَجْتَمِعُ اجْتِمَاعًا.

f: What is an example of the افْعَلَّ pattern?
b: احْمَرَّ يَحْمَرُّ احْمِرَارًا.

f: What are the six-letter augmented triliteral patterns mentioned?
b: اسْتَفْعَلَ، افْعَالَّ، افْعَوْعَلَ، افْعَنْلَلَ، افْعَنْلَى، افْعَوَّلَ.

f: What is an example of the اسْتَفْعَلَ pattern?
b: اسْتَخْرَجَ يَسْتَخْرِجُ اسْتِخْرَاجًا.

f: What is an example of the افْعَالَّ pattern?
b: احْمَارَّ يَحْمَارُّ احْمِيرَارًا.

f: What is an example of the افْعَوْعَلَ pattern?
b: اعْشَوْشَبَ يَعْشَوْشِبُ اعْشِيشَابًا.

f: What is an example of the افْعَنْلَلَ pattern?
b: اقْعَنْسَسَ يَقْعَنْسِسُ اقْعِنْسَاسًا.

f: What is an example of the افْعَنْلَى pattern?
b: اسْلَنْقَى يَسْلَنْقِي اسْلِنْقَاءً.

f: What is an example of the افْعَوَّلَ pattern?
b: اجْلَوَّذَ يَجْلَوِّذُ اجْلِوَّاذًا.

f: What are the three patterns of the augmented quadrilateral verb (الرباعي المزيد فيه) mentioned in the text?
b: تَفَعْلَلَ، افْعَنْلَلَ، افْعَلَلَّ.

f: What is an example of the augmented quadrilateral pattern تَفَعْلَلَ, including its present tense and verbal noun?
b: تَدَحْرَجَ يَتَدَحْرَجُ تَدَحْرُجًا.

f: What is an example of the augmented quadrilateral pattern افْعَنْلَلَ, including its present tense and verbal noun?
b: احْرَنْجَمَ يَحْرَنْجِمُ احْرِنْجَامًا.

f: What is an example of the augmented quadrilateral pattern افْعَلَلَّ, including its verbal noun?
b: اقْشَعَرَّ اقْشِعْرَارًا.

f: How is a transitive verb (الفعل المتعدي) defined in Arabic grammar?
b: It is a verb whose action passes from the subject to a direct object (المفعول به).

f: What is an example of a transitive verb, and what does it mean in terms of grammatical structure?
b: ضَرَبْتُ زَيْدًا — the action of “striking” passes from the subject تُ to the object زيدًا.

f: What other terms are used for a transitive verb (الفعل المتعدي)?
b: واقع and مجاوز.

f: How is an intransitive verb (الفعل غير المتعدي) defined?
b: It is a verb whose action does not pass beyond the subject to a direct object.

f: What is an example of an intransitive verb?
b: حَسُنَ زَيْدٌ.

f: What other terms are used for an intransitive verb (الفعل غير المتعدي)?
b: لازم and غير واقع.

f: By what means can a basic triliteral intransitive verb be made transitive according to the text?
b: By doubling the middle radical (تضعيف العين), by adding the hamzah, or by using a preposition.

f: How can the basic triliteral verb be made transitive through doubling of the middle radical (تضعيف العين)?
b: By changing the verb to the فَعَّلَ pattern, as in فَرَّحْتُ زَيْدًا.

f: How can the basic triliteral verb be made transitive through the addition of a hamzah?
b: By changing it to the أَفْعَلَ pattern, as in أَجْلَسْتُهُ.

f: How can an intransitive verb be made transitive through a preposition (حرف الجر)?
b: By attaching an appropriate preposition to the verb, as in ذَهَبْتُ بِزَيْدٍ and انْطَلَقْتُ بِهِ.

f: What is the definition of the past tense (الفعل الماضي) in Arabic grammar?
b: It is a verb that indicates a meaning that existed in past time.

f: How is the active/passive distinction expressed in the past tense according to the text?
b: The past tense is either built for the active subject (مبني للفاعل) or built for the passive object (مبني للمفعول), i.e. with the subject not named.

f: How is the past tense normally formed when it is built for the active subject (المبني للفاعل)?
b: Its first letter is fatḥah, or its first vowel-bearing letter is fatḥah.

f: What are the active past-tense forms of نَصَرَ for the different pronouns listed in the text?
b: نَصَرَ، نَصَرَا، نَصَرُوا، نَصَرَتْ، نَصَرَتَا، نَصَرْنَ، نَصَرْتَ، نَصَرْتُمَا، نَصَرْتُمْ، نَصَرْتِ، نَصَرْتُمَا، نَصَرْتُنَّ، نَصَرْتُ، نَصَرْنَا.

f: Which augmented verb patterns can be conjugated according to the active past-tense pattern exemplified by نَصَرَ?
b: أَفْعَلَ، فَعَّلَ، فَاعَلَ، فَعْلَلَ، تَفَعْلَلَ، تَفَاعَلَ، انْفَعَلَ، افْتَعَلَ، افْعَنْلَلَ، اسْتَفْعَلَ، افْعَلَلَّ، افْعَوْعَلَ، افْعَالَّ.

f: How should the initial alifs of augmented verb patterns be treated when determining their vowel patterns?
b: Their vowels should not be considered, because these alifs are extra (زائدة); they are pronounced at the beginning of speech but drop in connected speech.

f: What is the passive past tense (الماضي المبني للمفعول)?
b: It is the past-tense verb in which the doer/subject is not named (لم يُسمَّ فاعله).

f: How is the passive past tense formed when the verb's first letter is directly vowel-bearing?
b: Its first vowel-bearing letter is given ḍammah, while the letter before the final letter is given kasrah.

f: What are examples of passive past-tense patterns whose first letter is given ḍammah?
b: فُعِلَ، فُعْلِلَ، أُفْعِلَ، فُعِّلَ، فُوعِلَ، تُفُعِّلَ، تُفُوعِلَ، تُفُعْلِلَ.

f: Which passive past-tense patterns have the first vowel-bearing letter rather than the first written letter given ḍammah?
b: افْتُعِلَ and اسْتُفْعِلَ.

f: What happens to the hamzat al-waṣl (همزة الوصل) in a passive past-tense form such as اسْتُفْعِلَ?
b: It follows the vowel of the initial ḍammah: it is pronounced with ḍammah at the beginning of speech.

f: What vowel does the letter immediately before the final letter of a passive past-tense verb always take?
b: It is always given kasrah.

f: What are examples of passive past-tense verbs given in the text?
b: نُصِرَ زَيْدٌ and اسْتُخْرِجَ المالُ.

f: What is the present tense (الفعل المضارع) according to the text?
b: It is a verb beginning with one of the four present-tense prefixes (الزوائد الأربع): أ، ن، ت، ي.

f: What are the four present-tense prefixes in Arabic?
b: الهمزة، النون، التاء، الياء: أ، ن، ت، ي.

f: What mnemonic expression is given for the four present-tense prefixes?
b: أَنَيْتُ or أَتَيْنَ or نَأْتِي.

f: Which present-tense prefix is used for the first-person singular (المتكلم وحده)?
b: الهمزة (أ).

f: Which present-tense prefix is used for the first person when accompanied by someone else?
b: النون (ن).

f: Which present-tense prefix is used for the second person (المخاطب)?
b: التاء (ت), whether the addressee is singular, dual, or plural, and whether masculine or feminine.

f: Which present-tense prefix is used for the third-person feminine singular and dual?
b: التاء (ت).

f: Which present-tense prefix is used for the third-person masculine singular, dual, and plural?
b: الياء (ي).

f: Which present-tense prefix is used for the third-person feminine plural?
b: الياء (ي).

f: What persons can take the present-tense prefix تاء (تـ)?
b: The second person in its singular, dual, and plural forms, whether masculine or feminine; and the third-person feminine singular and dual.

f: What persons can take the present-tense prefix ياء (يـ)?
b: The third-person masculine singular, dual, and plural, and the third-person feminine plural.

f: What persons can take the present-tense prefix همزة (أ)?
b: The first-person singular only.

f: What persons can take the present-tense prefix نون (ن)?
b: The first person plural, i.e. the speaker together with others.

f: Can the Arabic present tense indicate both present and future time?
b: Yes. It can indicate present time (حال) or future time (استقبال).

f: What example illustrates the present tense indicating present time?
b: زَيْدٌ يَفْعَلُ الآنَ — “Zayd is doing it now.”

f: What example illustrates the present tense indicating future time?
b: زَيْدٌ يَفْعَلُ غَدًا — “Zayd will do it tomorrow.”

f: What happens to the temporal meaning of the Arabic present tense when سـ is prefixed to it?
b: It becomes restricted to future time.

f: What happens to the temporal meaning of the Arabic present tense when سوف precedes it?
b: It becomes restricted to future time.

f: What examples show the use of سـ and سوف to indicate the future?
b: سَيَفْعَلُ and سَوْفَ يَفْعَلُ.

f: What happens to the temporal meaning of the Arabic present tense when لام is prefixed to it, according to the text?
b: It becomes restricted to present time (حال).

f: What are the three patterns of the augmented quadrilateral verb (الرباعي المزيد فيه) given in the text?
b: تَفَعْلَلَ، افْعَنْلَلَ، افْعَلَلَّ.

f: What is an example of the augmented quadrilateral pattern تَفَعْلَلَ with its present tense and verbal noun?
b: تَدَحْرَجَ، يَتَدَحْرَجُ، تَدَحْرُجًا.

f: What is an example of the augmented quadrilateral pattern افْعَنْلَلَ with its present tense and verbal noun?
b: احْرَنْجَمَ، يَحْرَنْجِمُ، احْرِنْجَامًا.

f: What is an example of the augmented quadrilateral pattern افْعَلَلَّ with its verbal noun?
b: اقْشَعَرَّ، اقْشِعْرَارًا.

f: What is a transitive verb (الفعل المتعدي)?
b: A verb whose action passes from the subject (الفاعل) to a direct object (المفعول به).

f: What are the other terms for a transitive verb (الفعل المتعدي)?
b: واقع and مجاوز.

f: What is an example of a transitive verb passing from its subject to its direct object?
b: ضَرَبْتُ زَيْدًا.

f: What is an intransitive verb (الفعل غير المتعدي)?
b: A verb whose action does not pass from the subject to a direct object.

f: What are the other terms for an intransitive verb (الفعل غير المتعدي)?
b: لازم and غير واقع.

f: What is an example of an intransitive verb?
b: حَسُنَ زَيْدٌ.

f: By what three methods can a basic triliteral intransitive verb be made transitive?
b: By doubling its middle radical, adding hamzah, or using a preposition (حرف الجر).

f: How is a basic triliteral verb made transitive by doubling its middle radical?
b: By putting it on the فَعَّلَ pattern, e.g. فَرَّحْتُ زَيْدًا.

f: How is a basic triliteral verb made transitive by adding hamzah?
b: By putting it on the أَفْعَلَ pattern, e.g. أَجْلَسْتُهُ.

f: How can a verb be made transitive by using a preposition?
b: By attaching a suitable preposition, e.g. ذَهَبْتُ بِزَيْدٍ and انْطَلَقْتُ بِهِ.

f: What is the active present tense (المضارع المبني للفاعل) according to the text?
b: It is a present-tense verb whose present-tense prefix (حرف المضارعة) is generally fatḥah-vowelled.

f: What is the exception to the rule that the present-tense prefix of an active present verb is fatḥah-vowelled?
b: If the verb's past tense consists of four letters, its present-tense prefix is always ḍammah-vowelled.

f: What are examples of active present verbs whose past tense has four letters and whose present prefix is ḍammah-vowelled?
b: يُدَحْرِجُ، يُكْرِمُ، يُقَاتِلُ، يُفَرِّحُ.

f: What is the distinguishing feature of the active present tense for the four-letter past-tense verbs?
b: The letter before the final letter is always kasrah-vowelled.

f: What is the full present-tense conjugation of نَصَرَ in the active voice?
b: يَنْصُرُ، يَنْصُرَانِ، يَنْصُرُونَ؛ تَنْصُرُ، تَنْصُرَانِ، يَنْصُرْنَ؛ تَنْصُرُ، تَنْصُرَانِ، تَنْصُرُونَ؛ تَنْصُرِينَ، تَنْصُرَانِ، تَنْصُرْنَ؛ أَنْصُرُ، نَنْصُرُ.

f: Which active present-tense forms are given as analogous to يَنْصُرُ?
b: يَضْرِبُ، يَعْلَمُ، يُدَحْرِجُ، يُكْرِمُ، يُقَاتِلُ، يُفَرِّحُ، يَتَكَسَّرُ، يَتَبَاعَدُ، يَنْقَطِعُ، يَجْتَمِعُ، يَحْمَرُّ، يَحْمَارُّ، يَجْلَوِّذُ، يَسْتَخْرِجُ، يَعْشَوْشِبُ، يَقْعَنْسِسُ، يَسْلَنْقِي، يَتَدَحْرَجُ، يَحْرَنْجِمُ، يَقْشَعِرُّ.

f: What is the passive present tense (المضارع المبني للمفعول) according to the text?
b: It is a present-tense verb whose present-tense prefix is ḍammah-vowelled and whose letter before the final letter is fatḥah-vowelled.

f: What are examples of passive present-tense verbs?
b: يُنْصَرُ، يُدَحْرَجُ، يُكْرَمُ، يُفَرَّحُ، يُقَاتَلُ، يُسْتَخْرَجُ.

f: What happens to the form of the present tense when the negative particles ما or لا enter upon it?
b: They do not change its grammatical form.

f: What are the two negative particles that enter upon the Arabic present tense without changing its form?
b: ما and لا النافيتان.

f: What is the effect of لا النافية on the present-tense verb?
b: It negates the present tense without changing its form.

f: What is the effect of ما النافية on the present-tense verb?
b: It negates the present tense without changing its form.

f: What happens when a jussive particle (جازم) enters upon the present tense?
b: It removes the vowel ending of the singular masculine and singular feminine third-person forms, and removes the nūn from the dual, masculine plural, and feminine singular second-person forms.

f: Which nūn does the jussive particle not remove?
b: It does not remove the nūn of the feminine plural, because that nūn is a pronoun, analogous to the wāw of the masculine plural.

f: What happens to the nūn of the feminine plural when a jussive particle enters the present tense?
b: It remains in place in every case, because it is a pronoun.

f: What is the jussive conjugation of يَنْصُرُ in the third-person masculine forms?
b: لَمْ يَنْصُرْ، لَمْ يَنْصُرَا، لَمْ يَنْصُرُوا.

f: What is the jussive conjugation of يَنْصُرُ in the third-person feminine forms?
b: لَمْ تَنْصُرْ، لَمْ تَنْصُرَا، لَمْ يَنْصُرْنَ.

f: What is the jussive conjugation of يَنْصُرُ in the second-person masculine forms?
b: لَمْ تَنْصُرْ، لَمْ تَنْصُرَا، لَمْ تَنْصُرُوا.

f: What is the jussive conjugation of يَنْصُرُ in the second-person feminine forms?
b: لَمْ تَنْصُرِي، لَمْ تَنْصُرَا، لَمْ تَنْصُرْنَ.

f: What are the first-person jussive forms of يَنْصُرُ?
b: لَمْ أَنْصُرْ، لَمْ نَنْصُرْ.

f: What happens when an accusative/subjunctive particle (ناصب) enters upon the present tense?
b: It changes the ḍammah to a fatḥah and removes the nūns, except for the nūn of the feminine plural.

f: Which nūn remains when an accusative/subjunctive particle enters upon the present tense?
b: The nūn of the feminine plural remains because it is a pronoun.

f: What are examples of the present tense after the accusative particle لَنْ?
b: لَنْ يَنْصُرَ، لَنْ يَنْصُرَا، لَنْ يَنْصُرُوا، لَنْ تَنْصُرَ، لَنْ تَنْصُرَا، لَنْ يَنْصُرْنَ.

f: What is the grammatical function of لام الأمر when it enters upon the present tense?
b: It is a jussive particle (جازم) and makes the present tense jussive.

f: How is لام الأمر used to command an absent masculine singular?
b: لِيَنْصُرْ.

f: How is لام الأمر used with the absent masculine dual and plural?
b: لِيَنْصُرَا، لِيَنْصُرُوا.

f: How is لام الأمر used with the absent feminine singular and plural?
b: لِتَنْصُرْ، لِيَنْصُرْنَ.

f: What are examples of other verbs made jussive by لام الأمر?
b: لِيَضْرِبْ، لِيَعْلَمْ، لِيَدْخُلْ، لِيُدَحْرِجْ.

f: What is the grammatical function of لا الناهية when it enters upon the present tense?
b: It is a jussive particle that makes the present tense jussive and expresses prohibition.

f: How is لا الناهية used to prohibit an absent masculine singular from doing something?
b: لا يَنْصُرْ.

f: How is لا الناهية used with the absent masculine dual and plural?
b: لا يَنْصُرَا، لا يَنْصُرُوا.

f: How is لا الناهية used with the absent feminine singular and plural?
b: لا تَنْصُرْ، لا يَنْصُرْنَ.

f: How is لا الناهية used to prohibit a present masculine singular from doing something?
b: لا تَنْصُرْ.

f: How is لا الناهية used with the second-person masculine dual and plural?
b: لا تَنْصُرَا، لا تَنْصُرُوا.

f: How is لا الناهية used with the second-person feminine singular, dual, and plural?
b: لا تَنْصُرِي، لا تَنْصُرَا، لا تَنْصُرْنَ.

f: What is the imperative verb (فعل الأمر) referred to as أمر الحاضر?
b: It is the command directed to the person being addressed.

f: How is the Arabic imperative formed in relation to the jussive present tense?
b: It follows the form of the jussive present tense.

f: How is the imperative formed when the letter immediately after the present-tense prefix is vowelled?
b: The present-tense prefix is removed, and the remaining form is made jussive.

f: What is the imperative conjugation of تُدَحْرِجُ when the letter after the present-tense prefix is vowelled?
b: دَحْرِجْ، دَحْرِجَا، دَحْرِجُوا؛ دَحْرِجِي، دَحْرِجَا، دَحْرِجْنَ.

f: What imperative forms are given as analogous to دَحْرِجْ?
b: فَرِّحْ، قَاتِلْ، تَكَسَّرْ، تَبَاعَدْ، تَدَحْرَجْ.

f: How is the imperative formed when the letter immediately after the present-tense prefix is sukūn-vowelled?
b: The present-tense prefix is removed, the remaining form is made jussive, and a kasrah-vowelled hamzat al-waṣl is added at the beginning.

f: When is the hamzat al-waṣl added to the beginning of an imperative with a sukūn after the present-tense prefix?
b: When removing the present-tense prefix would leave the imperative beginning with a sukūn, making an initial hamzat al-waṣl necessary.

f: When is the hamzat al-waṣl of the imperative given ḍammah instead of kasrah?
b: When the middle radical of the present tense is ḍammah-vowelled.

f: What is the imperative conjugation of يَنْصُرُ when the present-tense prefix is removed and hamzat al-waṣl is added?
b: اُنْصُرْ، اُنْصُرَا، اُنْصُرُوا؛ اُنْصُرِي، اُنْصُرَا، اُنْصُرْنَ.

f: What is the imperative of يَضْرِبُ?
b: اضْرِبْ.

f: What is the imperative of يَعْلَمُ?
b: اعْلَمْ.

f: What is the imperative of يَنْقَطِعُ?
b: انْقَطِعْ.

f: What is the imperative of يَجْتَمِعُ?
b: اجْتَمِعْ.

f: What is the imperative of يَسْتَخْرِجُ?
b: اسْتَخْرِجْ.

f: Why is the hamzah in أَكْرِمْ pronounced with fatḥah according to the text?
b: The fatḥah is based on a rejected/underlying original form (الأصل المرفوض): the supposed original form of تُكْرِمُ is تُؤَكْرِمُ.

f: When two tāʾs (تاءان) occur at the beginning of the present tense of a verb on the patterns تَفَعَّلَ، تَفَاعَلَ، or تَفَعْلَلَ, what two options are permitted?
b: Both tāʾs may be retained, or one of them may be deleted.

f: What are examples of retaining both tāʾs when two tāʾs occur at the beginning of a present-tense verb?
b: تَتَجَنَّبُ، تَتَقَاتَلُ، تَتَدَحْرَجُ.

f: What are examples from the Qur'an of deleting one tāʾ when two tāʾs occur at the beginning of a present-tense verb?
b: فَأَنْتَ لَهُ تَصَدَّى، تَلَظَّى، تَنَزَّلُ الْمَلَائِكَةُ.

f: When is the tāʾ of the pattern افْتَعَلَ changed into a ṭāʾ (ط)?
b: When the first radical (فاء الفعل) is ص، ض، ط، or ظ.

f: What happens to the tāʾ of افْتَعَلَ when its first radical is ص، ض، ط، or ظ?
b: The tāʾ is changed into ṭāʾ (ط).

f: What is the افْتَعَلَ form derived from الصُّلْح?
b: اصْطَلَحَ.

f: What is the افْتَعَلَ form derived from الضَّرْب?
b: اضْطَرَبَ.

f: What is the افْتَعَلَ form derived from الطَّرْد?
b: اطَّرَدَ.

f: What is the افْتَعَلَ form derived from الظُّلْم?
b: اظْطَلَمَ.

f: What are the main derived forms of اصْطَلَحَ given in the text?
b: اصْطَلَحَ، يَصْطَلِحُ، اصْطِلَاحًا، مُصْطَلِحٌ، مُصْطَلَحٌ عَلَيْهِ، اصْطَلِحْ، لا تَصْطَلِحْ.

f: What is the present tense of اصْطَلَحَ?
b: يَصْطَلِحُ.

f: What is the verbal noun of اصْطَلَحَ?
b: اصْطِلَاحًا.

f: What is the active participle of اصْطَلَحَ?
b: مُصْطَلِحٌ.

f: What is the passive participle of اصْطَلَحَ?
b: مُصْطَلَحٌ عَلَيْهِ.

f: What is the imperative of اصْطَلَحَ?
b: اصْطَلِحْ.

f: What is the prohibitive form of اصْطَلَحَ?
b: لا تَصْطَلِحْ.

f: When is the tāʾ of the pattern افْتَعَلَ changed into a dāl (د)?
b: When the first radical (فاء الفعل) is د، ذ، or ز.

f: What happens to the tāʾ of افْتَعَلَ when its first radical is د، ذ، or ز?
b: The tāʾ is changed into dāl (د).

f: What is the افْتَعَلَ form derived from الدَّرْء?
b: ادَّرَأَ.

f: What is the افْتَعَلَ form derived from الذِّكْر?
b: اذَّكَرَ.

f: What is the افْتَعَلَ form derived from الزَّجْر?
b: ازْدَجَرَ.

f: When are the wāw, yāʾ, or thāʾ at the beginning of افْتَعَلَ changed into tāʾ?
b: When the first radical (فاء الفعل) is و، ي، or ث.

f: What happens when the first radical of افْتَعَلَ is wāw, yāʾ, or thāʾ?
b: The wāw, yāʾ, or thāʾ is changed into tāʾ, and that tāʾ is then assimilated into the tāʾ of افْتَعَلَ.

f: What is an example of the change involving a wāw as the first radical of افْتَعَلَ?
b: اتَّقى.

f: What is an example of the change involving a yāʾ as the first radical of افْتَعَلَ?
b: اتَّسَرَ.

f: What is an example of the change involving a thāʾ as the first radical of افْتَعَلَ?
b: اتَّغَرَ.

f: What are the two types of nūn of emphasis (نون التأكيد)?
b: The light nūn (النون الخفيفة), which is sākin, and the heavy nūn (النون الثقيلة), which is fatḥah-vowelled.

f: Which verbs can take the nūns of emphasis (نون التأكيد)?
b: Verbs other than the past tense, i.e. the non-past forms, with the specific exceptions mentioned for certain forms.

f: What is the vowel of the light nūn of emphasis (نون التأكيد الخفيفة)?
b: It is sākin (نْ).

f: What is the vowel of the heavy nūn of emphasis (نون التأكيد الثقيلة)?
b: It is fatḥah-vowelled (نَّ).

f: Which forms have a special treatment with the nūns of emphasis?
b: The dual forms in all cases and the feminine plural forms.

f: How are the two nūns of emphasis pronounced with the dual form?
b: They are fatḥah-vowelled/connected as نِّ after the dual ending, e.g. اذْهَبَانِّ.

f: How are the two nūns of emphasis pronounced with the feminine plural?
b: They are kasrah-vowelled, e.g. اذْهَبْنَانِّ.

f: Why is an alif inserted after the nūn of the feminine plural before the nūn of emphasis?
b: To separate the two nūns and prevent them from directly meeting.

f: Why is the light nūn of emphasis not attached to the feminine plural form?
b: Because doing so would result in the impermissible meeting of two sukūns.

f: When is the meeting of two sukūns permitted in Arabic according to the text?
b: It is permitted when the first is a long-vowel letter (حرف مد) and the second is assimilated (مدغم), as in دَابَّةٌ and وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ.

f: What happens to the nūn of the five special present-tense forms (الأمثلة الخمسة) when a nūn of emphasis is attached?
b: The nūn of the five forms is deleted.

f: Which five present-tense forms are known as الأمثلة الخمسة in the text?
b: يَفْعَلَانِ، تَفْعَلَانِ، يَفْعَلُونَ، تَفْعَلُونَ، تَفْعَلِينَ.

f: Which additional letters are deleted from the masculine plural forms when a nūn of emphasis is attached?
b: The wāw of يَفْعَلُونَ and تَفْعَلُونَ is deleted.

f: Which additional letter is deleted from the feminine singular form when a nūn of emphasis is attached?
b: The yāʾ of تَفْعَلِينَ is deleted.

f: When is the wāw or yāʾ of the five forms retained despite the attachment of the nūn of emphasis?
b: It is retained when the letter before it has fatḥah, as in لا تَخْشَوُنَّ، لا تَخْشَيِنَّ، لَتُبْلَوُنَّ، فَإِمَّا تَرَيِنَّ.

f: What happens to the final vowel of a verb when the heavy or light nūn of emphasis is attached?
b: It is fatḥah for the third-person masculine/feminine singular, ḍammah for the masculine plural, and kasrah for the second-person feminine singular.

f: What is the fully emphasized heavy-nūn form of the jussive command for the absent masculine singular, dual, and plural of يَنْصُرُ?
b: لِيَنْصُرَنَّ، لِيَنْصُرَانِّ، لِيَنْصُرُنَّ.

f: What is the fully emphasized heavy-nūn form of the jussive command for the absent feminine singular and plural of تَنْصُرُ/يَنْصُرْنَ?
b: لِتَنْصُرَنَّ، لِتَنْصُرَانِّ، لِيَنْصُرْنَانِّ.

f: What are the corresponding light-nūn forms of the emphasized command for the absent masculine singular and plural?
b: لِيَنْصُرَنْ، لِيَنْصُرُنْ.

f: What is the fully emphasized heavy-nūn imperative of يَنْصُرُ for the second-person masculine singular, dual, and plural?
b: انْصُرَنَّ، انْصُرَانِّ، انْصُرُنَّ.

f: What is the fully emphasized heavy-nūn imperative of يَنْصُرُ for the second-person feminine singular, dual, and plural?
b: انْصُرِنَّ، انْصُرَانِّ، انْصُرْنَانِّ.

f: What are the corresponding light-nūn imperative forms for the second-person masculine singular, plural, and feminine singular?
b: انْصُرَنْ، انْصُرُنْ، انْصُرِنْ.

f: What is the most common pattern for the active participle (اسم الفاعل) of a basic triliteral verb (الثلاثي المجرد)?
b: It is فَاعِل.

f: What are the singular, dual, plural, feminine, and broken-plural forms of the active participle نَاصِر?
b: Masculine: نَاصِرٌ، نَاصِرَانِ، نَاصِرُونَ. Feminine: نَاصِرَةٌ، نَاصِرَتَانِ، نَاصِرَاتٌ. Broken plural: نَوَاصِرٌ.

f: What is the most common pattern for the passive participle (اسم المفعول) of a basic triliteral verb (الثلاثي المجرد)?
b: It is مَفْعُول.

f: What are the singular, dual, plural, feminine, and broken-plural forms of the passive participle مَنْصُور?
b: Masculine: مَنْصُورٌ، مَنْصُورَانِ، مَنْصُورُونَ. Feminine: مَنْصُورَةٌ، مَنْصُورَتَانِ، مَنْصُورَاتٌ. Broken plural: مَنَاصِرُ.

f: How is a passive participle that governs through a preposition declined according to the text?
b: The passive participle itself does not change for number or gender; instead, the pronoun attached after the preposition changes.

f: What examples illustrate the unchanged passive participle with different pronouns after a preposition?
b: مَمْرُورٌ بِهِ، مَمْرُورٌ بِهِمَا، مَمْرُورٌ بِهِمْ؛ مَمْرُورٌ بِهَا، مَمْرُورٌ بِهِمَا، مَمْرُورٌ بِهِنَّ. The passive participle مَمْرُورٌ remains unchanged, while the pronoun varies according to number and gender.

f: Can the pattern فَعِيل have the meaning of an active participle?
b: Yes. فَعِيل can sometimes have the meaning of the active participle, such as الرَّحِيم meaning الرَّاحِم (“the merciful / one who shows mercy”).

f: Can the pattern فَعِيل have the meaning of a passive participle?
b: Yes. فَعِيل can sometimes have the meaning of the passive participle, such as القَتِيل meaning المَقْتُول (“the slain / the one who was killed”).

f: How are the active and passive participles of verbs with more than three letters formed?
b: In the present tense, replace the present-tense prefix with a ḍammah-vowelled mīm (مُـ). For the active participle, give the letter before the final letter a kasrah; for the passive participle, give it a fatḥah.

f: How are the active and passive participles of أَكْرَمَ formed?
b: مُكْرِمٌ = active participle (“one who honors”), and مُكْرَمٌ = passive participle (“one who is honored”).

f: How are the active and passive participles of دَحْرَجَ formed?
b: مُدَحْرِجٌ = active participle, and مُدَحْرَجٌ = passive participle.

f: How are the active and passive participles of اِسْتَخْرَجَ formed?
b: مُسْتَخْرِجٌ = active participle, and مُسْتَخْرَجٌ = passive participle.

f: How are the active and passive participles of تَدَحْرَجَ formed?
b: مُتَدَحْرِجٌ = active participle, and مُتَدَحْرَجٌ = passive participle.

f: Can the active and passive participles of verbs with more than three letters sometimes have the same written form?
b: Yes. In some cases the active and passive participles are identical in form, and the intended meaning is determined by the context and grammatical interpretation.

f: What examples does the text give where the active and passive participles have the same form?
b: مُحَابٌّ، مُتَحَابٌّ، مُخْتَارٌ، مُنْقَادٌ، مُضْطَرٌّ، مُعْتَدٌّ، مُنْصَبٌّ، مُنْصَبٌّ فِيهِ، مُنْجَابٌّ، مُنْجَابٌّ عَنْهُ.

f: What does the text mean when it says that the “ تقدير ” differs when the active and passive participles have the same form?
b: Although the wording/form is the same, the underlying grammatical interpretation or intended meaning differs according to the context.

f: What is the المضاعف (doubled verb) also called, and why?
b: It is called الأَصَمّ (“the deaf one”) because of its strength/heaviness in pronunciation.

f: What is the doubled basic triliteral verb (المضاعف من الثلاثي المجرد)?
b: It is a triliteral verb whose second and third root letters are of the same type, such as رَدَّ. Its underlying form is رَدَدَ.

f: How is رَدَّ derived from رَدَدَ?
b: The first دال is made sākin (رَدْدَ) and then assimilated into the second dāl, producing رَدَّ.

f: What is the doubled augmented verb (المزيد فيه)?
b: It is a verb in which the second and third root letters (ʿayn and lām) are of the same type, such as رَدَّ and أَعَدَّ. Their underlying forms are رَدَدَ and أَعْدَدَ.

f: What is the doubled quadrilateral verb (المضاعف من الرباعي)?
b: It is a quadrilateral verb in which the first and third root positions (فاء and لام الأولى) are of the same type, and the second and fourth positions (عين and لام الثانية) are also of the same type.

f: What is another name for the doubled quadrilateral verb?
b: It is also called المُطَابِق.

f: What is an example of the doubled quadrilateral verb?
b: زَلْزَلَ يُزَلْزِلُ زَلْزَلَةً وزِلْزَالًا.

f: Why is the doubled verb treated together with the defective verbs (المعتلات)?
b: Because the doubled letter can undergo changes such as substitution and deletion, similar to changes that occur in defective verbs.

f: What example does the text give of substitution affecting the doubled letter?
b: أَمْلَيْتُ can be used with the meaning of أَمْلَلْتُ.

f: What examples does the text give of deletion affecting the doubled letter?
b: مِسْتُ، ظِلْتُ، أَحَسْتُ, which correspond respectively to مَسِسْتُ، ظَلِلْتُ، أَحْسَسْتُ.

f: What does مِسْتُ، ظِلْتُ، أَحَسْتُ mean according to the text?
b: مِسْتُ = مَسِسْتُ (“I touched”), ظِلْتُ = ظَلِلْتُ (“I remained/spent the day”), and أَحَسْتُ = أَحْسَسْتُ (“I perceived/felt”).

f: What is الإدغام in Arabic morphology?
b: Idghām is to make the first of two identical/consecutive letters sākin and merge it into the second.

f: What is the first letter in an idghām called?
b: The first letter is called مُدْغَمًا (“the assimilated/merged letter”).

f: What is the second letter in an idghām called?
b: The second letter is called مُدْغَمًا فِيهِ (“the letter into which it is merged”).

f: In which doubled verbs is idghām obligatory?
b: It is obligatory in forms such as مَدَّ يَمُدُّ، أَعَدَّ يُعِدُّ، اعْتَدَّ يَعْتَدُّ، انْقَدَّ يَنْقَدُّ، اسْوَدَّ يَسْوَدُّ، اسْوَادَّ يَسْوَادُّ، اسْتَعَدَّ يَسْتَعِدُّ، اطْمَأَنَّ يَطْمَئِنُّ، تَمَادَّ يَتَمَادُّ.

f: Is idghām obligatory in the passive voice of doubled verbs?
b: Yes. For example, مُدَّ يُمَدُّ. The same principle applies to analogous verbs.

f: Is idghām obligatory in the verbal noun of a doubled verb such as مَدَّ?
b: Yes. For example, the verbal noun مَدٌّ retains the assimilation.

f: What happens to idghām when an alif, wāw, or yāʾ of a pronoun is attached to a doubled verb?
b: Idghām remains obligatory. Examples are مَدَّا، مَدُّوا، مُدِّي.

f: In which forms is idghām prohibited for the doubled verb مَدَّ?
b: It is prohibited in forms such as مَدَدْتُ، مَدَدْنَا، مَدَدْتَ، مَدَدْتُنَّ، مَدَدْنَ، يَمْدُدْنَ، تَمْدُدْنَ، امْدُدْنَ، لَا تَمْدُدْنَ. In these forms, the two consonants must remain separated.

f: When is idghām optional after a jussive particle enters upon a singular doubled present-tense verb?
b: It is optional when the jussive particle enters upon the singular form. The exact vowel and whether assimilation is maintained or broken depends on the vowel of the verb's ʿayn in the present tense.

f: How is the jussive of a doubled verb with a kasrah on the ʿayn formed when idghām is maintained or broken?
b: With يَفِرُّ, one may say لَمْ يَفِرّ with idghām, or لَمْ يَفْرِرْ with the idghām broken.

f: How is the jussive of a doubled verb with a fatḥah on the ʿayn formed when idghām is maintained or broken?
b: With يَعَضُّ, one may say لَمْ يَعَضّ with idghām, or لَمْ يَعْضَضْ with the idghām broken.

f: What other verbs follow the same jussive rule as يَفِرُّ and يَعَضُّ?
b: Doubled verbs such as يَقْشَعِرُّ، يَحْمَرُّ، يَحْمَارُّ follow the same rule.

f: What happens when the ʿayn of the present tense of a doubled verb has a ḍammah?
b: All three vowel possibilities are permitted with the assimilated form, and the assimilation may also be broken. For example: لَمْ يَمُدّ and لَمْ يَمْدُدْ.

f: What happens to the doubled verb in the imperative?
b: The imperative follows the same basic rule as the jussive: assimilation may be maintained or broken where permitted by the relevant vowel.

f: How is the imperative of فَرَّ formed?
b: فِرَّ with idghām.

f: How is the imperative of عَضَّ formed?
b: عَضَّ with idghām.

f: How is the imperative of مَدَّ formed when idghām is maintained or broken?
b: مُدّ with idghām, or امْدُدْ with the idghām broken.

f: What is the active participle of مَدَّ?
b: مَادٌّ.

f: What are the dual and masculine plural forms of the active participle مَادٌّ?
b: مَادَّانِ (dual) and مَادُّونَ (masculine plural).

f: What are the feminine singular, dual, and plural forms of the active participle مَادٌّ?
b: مَادَّةٌ، مَادَّتَانِ، مَادَّاتٌ.

f: What is the broken plural of the active participle مَادٌّ?
b: مَوَادُّ.

f: What is the passive participle of مَدَّ?
b: مَمْدُودٌ, following the same pattern as مَنْصُورٌ.

f: What is the defective verb (المعتل) in Arabic morphology?
b: It is a verb in which one of its root letters is a weak letter (حرف علة): و، ي، ا. These are called the letters of lengthening and softness (حروف المد واللين).

f: What is the origin of the alif when it is counted as a weak root letter?
b: The alif is originally derived from either wāw or yāʾ; it is not originally an independent weak root letter.

f: How many types of defective verbs are there according to the text?
b: There are seven types.

f: What is a defective verb with a weak first root letter called?
b: It is called المعتل الفاء and is also called المثال.

f: Why is a verb with a weak first root letter called المثال?
b: It is called المثال because it resembles a sound verb in its ability to accept vowel movements.

f: What happens to an initial wāw in a basic triliteral verb whose present tense is on يَفْعِلُ with a kasrah on the ʿayn?
b: The initial wāw is deleted from the present tense.

f: What happens to an initial wāw in the verbal noun on the pattern فِعْلَة with a kasrah on the fāʾ?
b: The initial wāw is deleted.

f: When is the initial wāw of a wāw-initial defective verb preserved?
b: It is preserved in the other conjugated forms where the deletion conditions do not apply.

f: How is وَعَدَ conjugated in the forms illustrating deletion of the initial wāw?
b: وَعَدَ، يَعِدُ، عِدَةً، وَعْدًا، وَاعِدٌ، مَوْعُودٌ. The wāw is deleted in يَعِدُ and عِدَةً, but remains in the other forms shown.

f: What is the imperative and prohibition of وَعَدَ يَعِدُ?
b: Imperative: عِدْ. Prohibition: لَا تَعِدْ.

f: What other example does the text give of a wāw-initial defective verb whose wāw is deleted?
b: وَمِقَ يَمِقُ مِقَةً.

f: When is the deleted wāw of a wāw-initial defective verb restored?
b: It is restored when the kasrah following it is removed, as in لَمْ يُوعَدْ.

f: What happens to the initial wāw in the present tense pattern يَفْعَلُ with a fatḥah on the ʿayn?
b: It is preserved, as in وَجِلَ يَوْجَلُ.

f: What is the imperative of وَجِلَ يَوْجَلُ?
b: اِيجَلْ.

f: What is the original form of اِيجَلْ, and why did the wāw become a yāʾ?
b: Its original form is اَوْجَلْ. The wāw was changed to yāʾ because it was sākin while the preceding letter was kasrah.

f: What happens to the yāʾ in اِيجَلْ when the preceding letter becomes ḍammah?
b: The yāʾ is pronounced as a wāw, because a wāw is appropriate after a ḍammah. According to the text, it is pronounced with wāw but written with yāʾ: يا زَيْدُ ايْجَلْ.

f: What happens to the initial wāw in the present tense pattern يَفْعُلُ with a ḍammah on the ʿayn?
b: It is preserved, as in وَجُهَ يَوْجُهُ.

f: What are the imperative and prohibition of وَجُهَ يَوْجُهُ?
b: Imperative: أُوجُهْ. Prohibition: لَا تَوْجُهْ.

f: Why are the initial wāws deleted in يَطَأُ، يَسَعُ، يَضَعُ، يَقَعُ، يَدَعُ، يَهَبُ?
b: Their original present-tense pattern is يَفْعِلُ with a kasrah on the ʿayn. After deletion of the weak first letter, the ʿayn was opened because of the following guttural letter (حرف الحلق).

f: Why is the initial wāw deleted from يَذَرُ?
b: Because يَذَرُ has the same meaning as يَدَعُ, and therefore follows its pattern.

f: What does أَمَاتُوا represent in relation to يَدَعُ and يَذَرُ?
b: أَمَاتُوا is given as the past-tense form corresponding to يَدَعُ and يَذَرُ in the text's discussion.

f: What does deletion of the first root letter indicate about a defective verb?
b: Deletion of the first root letter is evidence that the verb is wāw-initial (واوي).

f: How does an initial yāʾ behave in the defective verb?
b: Unlike the initial wāw, the yāʾ remains in all circumstances.

f: What examples demonstrate that an initial yāʾ is retained?
b: يَمُنَ يَيْمُنُ، يَئِسَ يَيْأَسُ، يَسَرَ يَيْسِرُ.

f: How is the Form IV verb derived from a yāʾ-initial verb such as يَسَرَ?
b: أَيْسَرَ يُوسِرُ إِيسَارًا. Its active participle is مُوسِرٌ, and its passive participle is مُوسَرٌ.

f: Why does the yāʾ become wāw in the passive participle مُوسَرٌ of أَيْسَرَ?
b: Its original form is مُيْسَرٌ. The yāʾ changes into wāw because it is sākin and preceded by a ḍammah.

f: What happens to the initial yāʾ or wāw in Form VIII (افتعل) of a defective verb?
b: The initial weak letter is changed into tāʾ, and this tāʾ is assimilated into the tāʾ of افتعل.

f: What examples illustrate assimilation of a weak initial letter into the tāʾ of Form VIII?
b: اتَّعَدَ يَتَّعِدُ اتِّعَادًا، مُتَّعِدٌ، مُتَّعَدٌ and اتَّسَرَ يَتَّسِرُ اتِّسَارًا، مُتَّسِرٌ، مُتَّسَرٌ.

f: Are alternative forms without the assimilation found for Form VIII verbs beginning with a weak letter?
b: Yes. The text gives forms such as اَيْتَعَدَ يَاتَعِدُ، مُوتَعِدٌ، مُوتَعَدٌ and اَيْتَسَرَ يَاتَسِرُ، مُوتَسِرٌ، مُوتَسَرٌ بِهِ، مُوتَسَرٌ فِيهِ.

f: What is the rule for وَدَّ يَوَدُّ?
b: It follows the same rule as عَضَّ يَعَضُّ concerning its imperative and the treatment of its doubled letters.

f: What is the imperative of وَدَّ يَوَدُّ according to the text?
b: اِيدَدْ, analogous to اِعْضَضْ from عَضَّ يَعَضُّ.

f: What is a defective verb with a weak middle root letter called?
b: It is called المعتل العين and is also called الأجوف or ذو الثلاثة.

f: Why is a weak-middle verb called الأجوف?
b: Because its middle/root ʿayn is a weak letter, leaving the internal position of the word “hollow.”

f: Why is a weak-middle verb also called ذو الثلاثة?
b: Because its past tense can consist of three letters when speaking about oneself, as in قُلْتُ and بِعْتُ according to the text's terminology.

f: What happens to the middle weak letter of a basic triliteral hollow verb in the past tense?
b: It changes into an alif, whether the original weak letter is wāw or yāʾ, because the weak letter is vowelled and preceded by a fatḥah.

f: What examples illustrate a wāw-based and yāʾ-based hollow verb becoming alif in the past tense?
b: صَانَ comes from a wāw-based root, while بَاعَ comes from a yāʾ-based root.

f: What happens when a hollow past-tense verb is followed by the first-person, second-person, or feminine plural pronoun?
b: The past-tense pattern فَعَلَ changes: a wāw-based verb shifts to فَعُلَ, while a yāʾ-based verb shifts to فَعِلَ, revealing the original weak letter. The vowel is then transferred to the fāʾ and the weak middle letter is deleted because two sukūns would meet.

f: How is the wāw-based hollow verb صَانَ conjugated with attached pronouns?
b: صَانَ، صَانَا، صَانُوا؛ صَانَتْ، صَانَتَا، صُنَّ؛ صُنْتَ، صُنْتُمَا، صُنْتُمْ؛ صُنْتِ، صُنْتُمَا، صُنْتُنَّ؛ صُنْتُ، صُنَّا.

f: How is the yāʾ-based hollow verb بَاعَ conjugated with attached pronouns?
b: بَاعَ، بَاعَا، بَاعُوا؛ بَاعَتْ، بَاعَتَا، بِعْنَ؛ بِعْتَ، بِعْتُمَا، بِعْتُمْ؛ بِعْتِ، بِعْتُمَا، بِعْتُنَّ؛ بِعْتُ، بِعْنَا.

f: How is a hollow verb formed in the passive past tense?
b: The fāʾ is given a kasrah, and the hollow letter undergoes the appropriate defective-verb changes.

f: What is the passive past of the wāw-based hollow verb صَانَ?
b: صِينَ and its corresponding forms. Its defective change involves transfer (نقل) and substitution/change (قلب).

f: What is the passive past of the yāʾ-based hollow verb بَاعَ?
b: بِيعَ. Its defective change involves transfer (نقل).

f: How are the present-tense forms يَصُونُ and يَبِيعُ derived morphologically?
b: Their defective change is by transfer (نقل).

f: How are يَخَافُ and يَهَابُ defective in the present tense?
b: Their defective change involves both transfer (نقل) and substitution/change (قلب).

f: What happens when a jussive particle enters upon the present tense of a hollow verb?
b: The middle weak letter is deleted if the letter following it becomes sākin; it remains if the following letter is vowelled.

f: What are the jussive forms of يَصُونُ illustrating deletion of the middle weak letter?
b: لَمْ يَصُنْ، لَمْ يَصُونَا، لَمْ يَصُونُوا، لَمْ تَصُنْ، لَمْ تَصُونَا، لَمْ يَصُنَّ، لَمْ تَصُونِي، لَمْ أَصُنْ، لَمْ نَصُنْ, with the middle weak letter retained where the following element is vowelled.

f: How does the same jussive rule apply to the yāʾ-based hollow verb يَبِيعُ?
b: It follows the same rule: لَمْ يَبِعْ، لَمْ يَبِيعَا، لَمْ يَبِيعُوا and corresponding forms.

f: How does the same jussive rule apply to يَخَافُ?
b: It follows the same rule, e.g. لَمْ يَخَفْ، لَمْ يَخَافَا، لَمْ يَخَافُوا and corresponding forms.

f: How does the imperative of a hollow verb follow the jussive rule?
b: The same deletion rule applies. For صَانَ يَصُونُ: صُنْ، صُونَا، صُونُوا، صُونِي، صُونَا، صُنَّ.

f: What happens when the heavy nūn of emphasis (نون التوكيد الثقيلة) is attached to the hollow verb صَانَ يَصُونُ?
b: The forms include صُونَنَّ، صُونَانِّ، صُونُنَّ، صُونِنَّ، صُونَانِّ، صُنْنَانِّ.

f: What happens when the light nūn of emphasis (نون التوكيد الخفيفة) is attached to صَانَ يَصُونُ?
b: Forms include صُونَنْ، صُونُنْ، صُونِنْ and corresponding forms.

f: What are the ordinary imperative forms of the hollow verbs بَاعَ and خَافَ shown in the text?
b: بِعْ، بِيعا، بِيعُوا، بِيعِي، بِيعا، بِعْنَ and خَفْ، خَافَا، خَافُوا، خَافِي، خَافَا، خَفْنَ.

f: What are the heavy-nūn forms of emphasis for بَاعَ يَبِيعُ?
b: بِيعَنَّ، بِيعَانِّ، بِيعُنَّ، بِيعِنَّ، بِيعَانِّ، بِعْنَانِّ.

f: What are the heavy-nūn forms of emphasis for خَافَ يَخَافُ?
b: خَافَنَّ، خَافَانِّ، خَافُنَّ، خَافِنَّ، خَافَانِّ، خَفْنَانِّ.

f: What examples of the light nūn of emphasis are given for the hollow verbs صَانَ، بَاعَ، خَافَ?
b: صُونَنْ، بِيعَنْ، خَافَنْ, followed by their corresponding forms.

f: How many patterns of the augmented triliteral hollow verb (مزيد الثلاثي الأجوف) undergo defective changes according to the text?
b: Only four patterns are subject to the particular defective changes discussed.

f: What is the defective derivation of أَجَابَ يُجِيبُ إِجَابَةً?
b: Its original form is إِجْوَابًا. It undergoes transfer (نقل) and substitution/change (قلب). Two alifs then come together, so one is deleted and the tāʾ of the verbal noun pattern is supplied in compensation, producing إِجَابَةً.

f: What are the four augmented triliteral hollow verbs given in the text?
b: أَجَابَ يُجِيبُ إِجَابَةً، اسْتَقَامَ يَسْتَقِيمُ اسْتِقَامَةً، انْقَادَ يَنْقَادُ انْقِيَادًا، اخْتَارَ يَخْتَارُ اخْتِيَارًا.

f: How is the passive of أَجَابَ يُجِيبُ formed?
b: أُجِيبَ، يُجَابُ.

f: How is the passive of اسْتَقَامَ يَسْتَقِيمُ formed?
b: اسْتُقِيمَ، يُسْتَقَامُ.

f: How is the passive of انْقَادَ يَنْقَادُ formed?
b: انْقِيدَ، يُنْقَادُ.

f: How is the passive of اخْتَارَ يَخْتَارُ formed?
b: اخْتِيرَ، يُخْتَارُ.

f: What are the imperative forms of أَجَابَ، اسْتَقَامَ، انْقَادَ، اخْتَارَ?
b: أَجِبْ، أَجِيبَا، أَجِيبُوا؛ اسْتَقِمْ، اسْتَقِيمَا، اسْتَقِيمُوا؛ انْقَدْ، انْقَادَا، انْقَادُوا؛ اخْتَرْ، اخْتَارَا، اخْتَارُوا.

f: Which augmented triliteral verbs can remain sound despite containing a hollow root?
b: Examples include قَوَّلَ، تَقَوَّلَ، قَاوَلَ، تَقَاوَلَ، زَيَّنَ، تَزَيَّنَ، سَايَرَ، تَسَايَرَ، اسْوَدَّ، اسْوَادَّ، ابْيَضَّ، ابْيَاضَّ. The same applies to their other conjugated forms.

f: How is the active participle of a basic triliteral hollow verb formed?
b: Its hollow letter is changed into a hamzah, as in صَائِنٌ and بَائِعٌ.

f: How is the active participle of an augmented hollow verb formed?
b: It undergoes the same defective change as its present tense, e.g. مُجِيبٌ، مُسْتَقِيمٌ، مُنْقَادٌ، مُخْتَارٌ.

f: How is the passive participle of a basic triliteral hollow verb formed?
b: It undergoes transfer (نقل) and deletion (حذف), producing forms such as مَصُونٌ and مَبِيعٌ.

f: What does Sībawayh consider to be deleted in the passive participle مَصُونٌ?
b: According to Sībawayh, the deleted letter is the wāw of the passive-participle pattern (واو المفعول).

f: What does Abū al-Ḥasan al-Akhfash consider to be deleted in the passive participle of a hollow verb?
b: He considers the deleted letter to be the middle root letter (عين الفعل).

f: How do Banū Tamīm form the passive participle of a hollow verb such as بَاعَ?
b: They retain the yāʾ, saying مَبْيُوعٌ.

f: How is the passive participle of an augmented hollow verb formed when the verb itself undergoes defective changes?
b: It undergoes transfer (نقل) and substitution/change (قلب), producing forms such as مُجَابٌ، مُسْتَقَامٌ، مُنْقَادٌ، مُخْتَارٌ.

f: What is a defective verb with a weak final root letter called?
b: It is called المعتل اللام and is also called الناقص or ذو الأربعة.

f: Why is a weak-final verb called ذو الأربعة?
b: Because its past tense has four letters when conjugated in the first person, according to the terminology used in the text.

f: What happens to a wāw or yāʾ at the end of a basic triliteral defective verb when it is vowelled and preceded by a fatḥah?
b: It changes into alif.

f: What examples demonstrate the change of a final wāw or yāʾ into alif?
b: غَزَا، رَمَى، عَصَا، رَحَى.

f: Does the same final-weak-letter rule apply to verbs augmented beyond three letters?
b: Yes. Examples are أَعْطَى، اشْتَرَى، اسْتَقْصَى.

f: What are the passive participles of أَعْطَى، اشْتَرَى، اسْتَقْصَى?
b: مُعْطًى، مُشْتَرًى، مُسْتَقْصًى.

f: How is the passive present of a weak-final verb such as أَعْطَى formed?
b: When the agent is not named, the final weak letter remains in the passive present, e.g. يُعْطَى، يُشْتَرَى، يُغْزَى، يُرْمَى.

f: What happens to the final weak letter in the past tense of a weak-final verb in the pattern فَعَلُوا?
b: The final weak letter is always deleted.

f: When is the final weak letter deleted in the past-tense forms فَعَلَتْ and فَعَلَتَا?
b: It is deleted when the ʿayn of the verb is fatḥah-vowelled.

f: When is the final weak letter retained in the past tense of a weak-final verb?
b: It is retained in the other forms where the conditions for deletion are absent.

f: How is غَزَا conjugated in the past tense?
b: غَزَا، غَزَوَا، غَزَوْا؛ غَزَتْ، غَزَتَا، غَزَوْنَ؛ غَزَوْتَ، غَزَوْتُمَا، غَزَوْتُمْ؛ غَزَوْتِ، غَزَوْتُمَا، غَزَوْتُنَّ؛ غَزَوْتُ، غَزَوْنَا.

f: How is رَمَى conjugated in the past tense?
b: رَمَى، رَمَيَا، رَمَوْا؛ رَمَتْ، رَمَتَا، رَمَيْنَ؛ رَمَيْتَ، رَمَيْتُمَا، رَمَيْتُمْ؛ رَمَيْتِ، رَمَيْتُمَا، رَمَيْتُنَّ؛ رَمَيْتُ، رَمَيْنَا.

f: How is رَضِيَ conjugated in the past tense?
b: رَضِيَ، رَضِيَا، رَضُوا؛ رَضِيَتْ، رَضِيَتَا، رَضِينَ؛ رَضِيتَ، رَضِيتُمَا، رَضِيتُمْ؛ رَضِيتِ، رَضِيتُمَا، رَضِيتُنَّ؛ رَضِيتُ، رَضِينَا.

f: How is سَرُوَ conjugated in the past tense?
b: سَرُوَ، سَرُوَا، سَرُوا؛ سَرُوَتْ، سَرُوَتَا، سَرُونَ؛ سَرُوتَ، سَرُوتُمَا، سَرُوتُمْ؛ سَرُوتِ، سَرُوتُمَا، سَرُوتُنَّ؛ سَرُوتُ، سَرُونَا.

f: Why is the vowel before the masculine plural wāw fatḥah in غَزَوْا and رَمَوْا?
b: When the wāw of the pronoun attaches to a weak-final verb after deletion of the final weak letter, if the preceding vowel is a fatḥah, the fatḥah is retained.

f: Why is the vowel before the masculine plural wāw ḍammah in رَضُوا and سَرُوا?
b: If the letter before the pronoun's wāw originally has a ḍammah or kasrah, it is changed to ḍammah after deletion of the final weak letter.

f: What is the underlying form of رَضُوا, and how does it become رَضُوا?
b: Its underlying form is رَضِيُوا. The ḍammah of the yāʾ is transferred to the preceding ḍād, and the yāʾ is then deleted because two sukūns would meet, producing رَضُوا.

f: What happens to the final weak letter of a weak-final verb in the indicative present tense (الرفع)?
b: The wāw, yāʾ, or alif is made sākin, according to the text's description.

f: What happens to the final weak letter of a weak-final verb in the jussive (الجزم)?
b: The final weak letter is deleted.

f: What happens to a final wāw or yāʾ in the subjunctive/accusative (النصب)?
b: The wāw or yāʾ is given a fatḥah.

f: What happens to the final alif of a weak-final verb in the subjunctive/accusative?
b: The alif remains, just as it does in the indicative.

f: What happens to the nūns of the five verbs (الأفعال الخمسة) when a jussive or subjunctive particle enters upon a weak-final verb?
b: The nūns are deleted, except for the nūn of the feminine plural.

f: What are examples of the jussive forms of يَغْزُو?
b: Examples include لَمْ يَغْزُ، لَمْ يَغْزُوَا، لَمْ يَغْزُوا and the corresponding feminine and first-person forms given in the text.

f: What are examples of the jussive forms of يَرْمِي?
b: لَمْ يَرْمِ، لَمْ يَرْمِيَا، لَمْ يَرْمُوا and corresponding forms.

f: What are examples of the jussive forms of يَرْضَى?
b: لَمْ يَرْضَ، لَمْ يَرْضَيَا، لَمْ يَرْضَوْا and corresponding forms.

f: What are examples of the subjunctive forms of weak-final verbs given in the text?
b: لَنْ يَغْزُوَ، لَنْ يَغْزُوا، لَنْ يَرْمِيَ، لَنْ يَرْضَى.

f: In which present-tense forms is the final weak letter retained?
b: It is retained in the dual forms and the feminine plural forms.

f: In which present-tense forms is the final weak letter deleted?
b: It is deleted in the masculine plural and the second-person feminine singular forms.

f: How is يَغْزُو conjugated in the indicative present tense?
b: يَغْزُو، يَغْزُوَانِ، يَغْزُونَ؛ تَغْزُو، تَغْزُوَانِ، يَغْزُونَ؛ تَغْزُو، تَغْزُوَانِ، تَغْزُونَ؛ تَغْزِينَ، تَغْزُوَانِ، تَغْزُونَ؛ أَغْزُو، نَغْزُو.

f: What happens to the final weak letter in the masculine plural of يَغْزُو?
b: The final wāw of the verb is deleted, leaving يَغْزُونَ with the wāw of the plural ending.

f: How do the masculine and feminine plural forms of a weak-final verb sometimes become identical in pronunciation or writing?
b: The surface form can be the same, but their underlying morphological analyses differ; the text says ويستوي فيه لفظ جماعة الذكور والإناث... ويختلف التقدير.

f: What are the morphological patterns of the masculine plural present forms of a weak-final verb?
b: The masculine plural patterns are يَفْعُونَ and تَفْعُونَ.

f: What are the morphological patterns of the feminine plural present forms of a weak-final verb?
b: The feminine plural patterns are يَفْعُلْنَ and تَفْعُلْنَ.

f: How is يَرْمِي conjugated in the indicative present tense?
b: يَرْمِي، يَرْمِيَانِ، يَرْمُونَ؛ تَرْمِي، تَرْمِيَانِ، يَرْمِينَ؛ تَرْمِي، تَرْمِيَانِ، تَرْمُونَ؛ تَرْمِينَ، تَرْمِيَانِ، تَرْمِينَ؛ أَرْمِي، نَرْمِي.

f: What is the underlying form of يَرْمُونَ, and how does it become يَرْمُونَ?
b: Its underlying form is يَرْمِيُونَ. It undergoes the same type of changes as رَضُوا: the vowel is transferred and the yāʾ is deleted because of the meeting of two sukūns.

f: What rule applies to weak-final verbs whose letter before the final weak letter has a kasrah?
b: They follow the same pattern as يُهْدِي، يُنَاجِي، يَرْتَجِي، يَنْبَرِي، يَسْتَدْعِي، يَرْعَوِي، يَعْرَوْرِي. Their conjugation follows the yāʾ-final pattern illustrated by يَرْمِي.

f: How is يَرْضَى conjugated in the indicative present tense?
b: يَرْضَى، يَرْضَيَانِ، يَرْضَوْنَ؛ تَرْضَى، تَرْضَيَانِ، يَرْضَيْنَ؛ تَرْضَى، تَرْضَيَانِ، تَرْضَوْنَ؛ تَرْضَيْنَ، تَرْضَيَانِ، تَرْضَيْنَ؛ أَرْضَى، نَرْضَى.

f: What rule applies to weak-final verbs whose letter before the final weak letter has a fatḥah?
b: They follow the same pattern as يَتَمَطَّى، يَتَصَابَى، يَتَصَدَّى، يَتَقَلْسَى.

f: How does the second-person feminine singular of يَرْمِي and يَرْضَى relate in form to the feminine plural?
b: Its surface wording resembles that of the feminine plural, but the underlying morphological analysis is different.

f: What are the morphological patterns of the second-person feminine singular of weak-final verbs?
b: For the yāʾ-final type, the patterns are تَفْعِينَ and تَفْعَيْنَ.

f: What are the morphological patterns of the feminine plural of weak-final verbs?
b: The patterns are تَفْعِلْنَ and تَفْعَلْنَ.

f: How is the imperative formed from a defective verb (الناقص)?
b: The final weak radical is deleted in the imperative according to the established conjugation rules. Examples: اغزُ، اغزُوا، اغزُوا، اغزِي، اغزُوا، اغزونَ; ارمِ، ارمِيا، ارمُوا، ارمِي، ارمِيا، ارمِينَ; ارضَ، ارضَيا، ارضَوا، ارضَي، ارضَيا، ارضَيْنَ.

f: What happens to the deleted final radical when the imperative of a defective verb takes the emphatic nūn (نون التوكيد)?
b: The deleted final radical is restored. Thus: اغزُوَنَّ، اغزُوانِّ؛ ارمِيَنَّ، ارمِيانِّ؛ ارضَيَنَّ، ارضَيانِّ.

f: How is the active participle (اسم الفاعل) formed from a defective verb?
b: Its final weak radical undergoes the appropriate change and is normally deleted in the indefinite singular masculine. Examples: غازٍ، غازِيانِ، غازُونَ؛ غازِيَةٌ، غازِيتانِ، غازِياتٌ؛ وغَوازٍ. Likewise: رامٍ and راضٍ.

f: Why is the final wāw of غازٍ changed into yāʾ?
b: Its original form is غازِوٌ. The final wāw is changed to yāʾ because it is at the end of the word and is preceded by a kasrah: غازِوٌ → غازِيٌ → غازٍ.

f: What analogous change occurs in the passive form غُزِيَ?
b: The wāw is likewise changed into yāʾ because it becomes final and is preceded by a kasrah: غُزِوَ → غُزِيَ.

f: Why is the feminine active participle غازية formed with yāʾ rather than wāw?
b: Because the feminine form is derived from the masculine, and the feminine tāʾ is an added suffix; therefore the change to yāʾ found in غازٍ is retained: غازية.

f: What is the passive participle of a wāw-final defective verb?
b: It is formed as مَغْزُوٌّ, e.g. from غزا.

f: What is the passive participle of a yāʾ-final defective verb?
b: It is formed as مَرْمِيٌّ, from رمى. Its underlying form is مَرْمُويٌ.

f: Why does مَرْمُويٌ become مَرْمِيٌّ?
b: The wāw is changed to yāʾ and the preceding letter is given kasrah. When a wāw and yāʾ occur together in one word, with the first being sākin, the wāw is changed into yāʾ and the two yāʾs are assimilated: مَرْمُويٌ → مَرْمُيٌ → مَرْمِيٌّ.

f: What are the forms of فَعُول derived from wāw-final and yāʾ-final roots?
b: From the wāw-final عدا: عَدُوٌّ. From the yāʾ-final بغى: بَغِيٌّ.

f: What are the forms of فَعِيل derived from wāw-final and yāʾ-final roots?
b: From the wāw-final: صَبِيٌّ; from the yāʾ-final: شَرِيٌّ.

f: What happens to the wāw of an augmented defective verb (المزيد فيه)?
b: A wāw occurring as the fourth radical or beyond is changed into yāʾ when the preceding letter is not ḍammah, because of the heaviness of the resulting word.

f: What examples illustrate the change of a fourth-or-later wāw into yāʾ in augmented defective verbs?
b: أعطى → يُعطي, اعتدى → يعتدي, استرشى → يسترشي. With attached pronouns: أعطيتُ، اعتديتُ، استرشيتُ; likewise تغازينا، تراجينا.

f: What is the fourth type of defective verb?
b: The fourth type is a verb defective in both its middle and final radicals, called اللَّفيف المقرون (the connected defective verb).

f: What are examples of the connected defective verb (اللفيف المقرون)?
b: Examples include شوى → يشوي → شيًّا, قوي → يقوى → قوة, روي → يروى → ريًّا, and رضي → يرضى → رضيًا.

f: What examples illustrate adjective formation from the connected defective root ر و ي?
b: رَيّانُ (well-watered/full), feminine رَيّا, analogous to عطشان/عطشى.

f: How is the Form IV verb from ر و ي conjugated?
b: أروى → يُروي → إرواءً, analogous to أعطى → يعطي.

f: How is the verb حيي conjugated?
b: حَيِيَ → يَحْيا → حياةً, analogous to رَضِيَ → يَرْضى. Its active participle is حَيٌّ.

f: How are the forms حيّا، حيّيا، حيّوا treated?
b: The forms are حَيّا، حَيِيا for the dual and حَيُّوا، حَيِيُوا for the plural; the plural means “they lived” and the active participle/adjective is أحياء. A lighter form حَيُوا is also permitted, analogous to رَضُوا.

f: What is the imperative of حيي?
b: اِحْيَ, analogous to ارضَ.

f: How is the Form IV verb أحيا conjugated?
b: أحيا → يُحيي → إحياءً, analogous to أعطى → يُعطي.

f: How is the Form III verb حايا conjugated?
b: حايا → يُحايي → مُحايَاةً.

f: How is the Form X verb استحيا conjugated, and what is its imperative?
b: استحيا → يستحيي → استحياءً; its imperative is استحيِ.

f: What alternative forms of استحيا are mentioned, and why does the shortened form occur?
b: Some speakers say استحى → يستحي → استحِ. The deletion is attributed to frequent usage (كثرة الاستعمال), analogous to لا أدرِ instead of لا أدري.

f: What is the fifth type of defective verb?
b: The fifth type is defective in both its initial and final radicals, called اللَّفيف المفروق (the separated defective verb).

f: What is the principal example of the separated defective verb (اللفيف المفروق)?
b: وقى → يقي.

f: How is the past tense of وقى conjugated?
b: وقى، وقَيا، وقَوا, analogous to رمى، رميا، رموا.

f: How is the present tense of وقى conjugated?
b: يقي، يقيانِ، يقونَ, analogous to يرمي، يرميانِ، يرمونَ.

f: What is the imperative of وقى?
b: The imperative is قِ, reduced to a single letter.

f: Why does قِ take the pronoun-like hāʾ in pausing?
b: Because the one-letter imperative قِ requires an additional hāʾ when pausing: قِهْ، قِيا، قُوا؛ قِي، قِيا، قِينَ.

f: How is the emphatic form of the imperative قِ formed with the heavy nūn?
b: قِيَنَّ، قِيانِّ، قُنَّ؛ قِنَّ، قِيانِّ، قِينانِّ.

f: What are the corresponding light-emphasis forms of قِ?
b: With the light emphatic nūn (نون التوكيد الخفيفة): قِيَنْ، قُنْ، قِنْ.

f: How is وجي conjugated?
b: وَجِيَ → يَوْجى, analogous to رَضِيَ → يَرْضى.

f: What is the imperative of وجي?
b: The imperative is اِيجَ, analogous to ارضَ.

f: What is the sixth type of defective verb?
b: The sixth type is defective in both its initial and middle radicals, as in يَيْنَ.

f: Where is the sixth type of defective verb found?
b: It occurs in certain nouns, such as يَوْمٌ and وَيْلٌ; no verb is constructed from this type according to the text.

f: What is the seventh type of defective verb?
b: The seventh type is defective in all three root positions—the initial, middle, and final radicals.

f: What is given as an example of the seventh type?
b: It is represented by the wāw and yāʾ used as the names of the two corresponding letters: واو and ياء.

f: How is the hamzated verb (المهموز) generally treated in its conjugation?
b: It is generally conjugated like a sound verb (الصحيح), because the hamzah is a sound radical. However, the hamzah may be lightened (تخفيف) when it is not the first radical because it is a strongly articulated letter from the deepest part of the throat.

f: How is أمل conjugated?
b: أمَلَ → يَأمُلُ, analogous to نصر → ينصر.

f: What is the imperative of أمَلَ?
b: أومُلْ, with the second hamzah changed into wāw.

f: Why is the second hamzah of أومُلْ changed into wāw?
b: When two hamzahs occur in one word and the second is sākin, the second hamzah must be changed into a weak letter corresponding to the vowel before it. Thus a preceding ḍammah produces wāw. Compare آمَنَ، أُومِنُ، إيمانٌ.

f: When two hamzahs meet, how is a second sākin hamzah treated?
b: It is changed according to the gender/type of the preceding vowel: fatḥah → alif, ḍammah → wāw, and kasrah → yāʾ.

f: What happens if the first of two hamzahs is a hamzat al-waṣl?
b: The second hamzah returns to its original hamzah pronunciation when connected if the preceding letter is fatḥah. Thus وأْمُلْ may occur when the word is joined in speech.

f: Which imperatives have their hamzah deleted irregularly because of frequent usage?
b: خُذْ، كُلْ، مُرْ. Their hamzah is deleted contrary to the regular rule because of their frequent use.

f: Can the original hamzah of مُرْ appear?
b: Yes. The original form can appear in connected speech: وأْمُرْ أَهْلَكَ بِالصَّلاةِ.

f: How is أزر conjugated, and what is its imperative?
b: أزَرَ → يَأْزِرُ; its imperative is إيْزَرْ.

f: How is هنأ conjugated, and what is its imperative?
b: هَنَأَ → يَهْنِئُ; its imperative is إيْنَئْ according to the pattern described for this class.

f: How is أدب conjugated, and what is its imperative?
b: أَدُبَ → يَأْدُبُ, analogous to كَرُمَ → يَكْرُمُ; its imperative is أُودُبْ.

f: How is سأل conjugated, and what is its imperative?
b: سَأَلَ → يَسْأَلُ, analogous to مَنَعَ → يَمْنَعُ; its imperative is اِسْأَلْ.

f: Can hamzated verbs undergo phonetic lightening (تخفيف)?
b: Yes. Several hamzated verbs have lighter forms in which the hamzah is changed or omitted, especially when this facilitates pronunciation.

f: What lighter form is given for سأل?
b: سالَ → يَسالُ → سَلْ.

f: How is آب conjugated?
b: آبَ → يَؤُوبُ.

f: How is ساء conjugated?
b: ساءَ → يَسُوءُ, analogous to the hollow verb صانَ → يَصُونُ.

f: How is جاء conjugated?
b: جاءَ → يَجِيءُ, analogous in its vowel pattern to كالَ → يَكِيلُ. Its active participle is جاءٍ.

f: What are the active participles of ساء and جاء?
b: ساءٍ and جاءٍ.

f: How is أسا conjugated?
b: أَسا → يَأْسُو, analogous to دعا → يدعو.

f: How is أتى conjugated, and what is its imperative?
b: أتى → يأتي, analogous to رمى → يرمي. Its imperative is ائتِ.

f: What shortened imperative of أتى is also reported?
b: Some speakers use تِ, by analogy with خُذْ, due to extreme shortening in frequent usage.

f: How is وأى conjugated?
b: وَأَى → يَئِي, analogous to وَقَى → يَقِي.

f: How is أوى conjugated?
b: أَوَى → يَأْوِي → أَيًّا, analogous to شَوَى → يَشْوِي → شَيًّا.

f: What is the imperative of أوى?
b: اِيوِ.

f: How is نأى conjugated?
b: نَأَى → يَنْأَى, analogous to رَعَى → يَرْعَى.

f: What is the regular pattern of رأى?
b: By analogy it would be رَأَى → يَرْأَى, following the pattern of نَأَى → يَنْأَى.

f: What exceptional change occurs in the present tense of رأى?
b: The Arabs unanimously deleted the hamzah from its present tense, producing يَرَى rather than يَرْأَى.

f: How is رأى conjugated in the present tense for the major pronouns?
b: يَرَى، يَرَيَانِ، يَرَوْنَ؛ تَرَى، تَرَيَانِ، يَرَيْنَ؛ تَرَى، تَرَيَانِ، تَرَوْنَ؛ تَرَيْنَ، تَرَيَانِ، تَرَيْنَ؛ أَرَى، نَرَى.

f: What happens in the feminine singular and feminine plural forms of رأى?
b: Their surface forms coincide in some positions, but their underlying morphological patterns differ. The feminine singular has the pattern تَفَيْنَ, whereas the feminine plural has تَفَلْنَ.

f: What are the two imperatives of رأى?
b: The original form is اِرْءَ, analogous to اِرْعَ; with deletion it becomes رَ.

f: What happens to the shortened imperative رَ when pausing?
b: It requires the hāʾ of pause: رَهْ. Its other forms are رَيا، رَوْا؛ رَيْ، رَيا، رَيْنَ.

f: How is the imperative of رأى emphasized with the heavy nūn?
b: رَيَنَّ، رَيانِّ، رَوُنَّ؛ رَيِنَّ، رَيانِّ، رَيْنانِّ.

f: How is the imperative of رأى emphasized with the light nūn?
b: رَيَنْ، رَوُنْ، رَيِنْ.

f: What is the active participle of رأى?
b: راءٍ، رائيانِ، راؤونَ, analogous to راعٍ، راعيانِ، راعونَ.

f: What is the passive participle of رأى?
b: مَرْئِيٌّ, analogous to مَرْعِيٌّ.

f: Why is the Form IV construction from رأى exceptional?
b: Its conjugation differs from the other Form IV verbs because the root contains the exceptional hamzah and weak radical sequence. It is أرى → يُري → إراءةً / إراءً / إرايةً.

f: What is the active participle of Form IV أرى?
b: مُرٍ، مُرِيانِ، مُرُونَ؛ مُرِيَةٌ، مُرِيتانِ، مُرِياتٌ.

f: What is the passive participle of Form IV أرى?
b: مُرًى، مُرَيانِ، مُرَوْنَ؛ مُراةٌ، مُراتانِ، مُرَياتٌ.

f: What is the imperative of أرى?
b: أَرِ، أَرِيا، أَرُوا؛ أَرِي، أَرِيا، أَرِينَ.

f: How is the imperative of أرى emphasized with the heavy nūn?
b: أَرِيَنَّ، أَرِيانِّ، أَرُنَّ؛ أَرِنَّ، أَرِيانِّ، أَرِينانِّ.

f: What is the prohibition (النهي) form of أرى?
b: لا تُرِ، لا تُرِيا، لا تُرُوا؛ لا تُرِي، لا تُرِيا، لا تُرِينَ.

f: How is the prohibition of أرى emphasized with the heavy nūn?
b: لا تُرِيَنَّ، لا تُرِيانِّ، لا تُرُنَّ؛ لا تُرِنَّ، لا تُرِيانِّ، لا تُرِينانِّ.

f: How is Form VIII formed from a verb whose first radical is hamzah?
b: The hamzah may be changed in the Form VIII construction. The text gives اِيتالَ analogous to اِخْتارَ, and اِيتَلى analogous to اِقْتَضى.

f: How are the active and passive participles generally formed from triliteral verbs for the names of time and place?
b: For triliteral verbs, the forms follow the patterns مَفْعِل or مَفْعَل, depending primarily on the vowel of the present-tense ʿayn and certain lexical exceptions.

f: When is the اسم الزمان والمكان formed on مَفْعِل with a kasrah?
b: When the present tense has a kasrah on its ʿayn, i.e. يَفْعِلُ: مَجْلِس from جلس and مَبِيت from بات.

f: When is the اسم الزمان والمكان normally formed on مَفْعَل with a fatḥah?
b: When the present tense has fatḥah or ḍammah on its ʿayn, i.e. يَفْعَلُ or يَفْعُلُ. Examples: مَذْهَب، مَقْتَل، مَشْرَب، مَقَام، مَدْبَغ.

f: Which words are anomalous in having a kasrah where the normal rule would predict a fatḥah in the اسم الزمان والمكان?
b: Examples include المَسْجِد، المَشْرِق، المَغْرِب، المَطْلِع، المَجْزِر، المَرْفِق، المَفْرِق، المَسْكِن، المَنْسِك، المَسْقِط، المَنْبِت.

f: Is the fatḥah pronunciation permitted in the anomalous forms of اسم الزمان والمكان?
b: A fatḥah has been transmitted for some of them, and the text states that fatḥah is permitted in all of them.

f: What is the rule for اسم الزمان والمكان when the verb has a sound first and final radical (صحيح الفاء واللام)?
b: The rules of مَفْعِل and مَفْعَل given above apply normally.

f: What is the rule for اسم الزمان والمكان from a verb defective in its first radical (معتل الفاء)?
b: Its ʿayn is always kasrah: مَوْضِع، مَوْعِد، مَوْسِم، مَوْجِل.

f: What is the rule for اسم الزمان والمكان from a verb defective in its final radical (معتل اللام)?
b: Its ʿayn is always fatḥah: مَأْوَى، مَرْمَى، مَرْوَى، مَقْوَى، مَرْعَى.

f: Can the اسم الزمان والمكان take the feminine tāʾ?
b: Yes. Some forms take tāʾ al-taʾnīth, such as مَظِنَّة، مَقْبَرَة، مَشْرَقَة.

f: What anomalous forms with ḍammah are reported for some feminine forms of اسم الزمان والمكان?
b: المَشْرُقَة and المَقْبُرَة are reported with ḍammah.

f: How are names of time and place formed from verbs with more than three radicals?
b: They follow the pattern of the passive participle (اسم المفعول). Examples are المُدْخَل and المُقام.

f: What pattern is used for a place in which something is abundant?
b: When something is abundant in a particular place, the pattern مَفْعَلَة is formed from the basic triliteral verb.

f: What examples illustrate the pattern مَفْعَلَة for places abundant in something?
b: أرضٌ مَسْبَعَةٌ = land abundant in lions; مَأْسَدَةٌ = place abundant in lions; مَذْأَبَةٌ = place abundant in wolves; مَبْطَخَةٌ = place abundant in kitchens/cooking; مَقْثَأَةٌ = place abundant in cucumbers.

f: What is اسم الآلة (the noun of instrument)?
b: It is a noun denoting the instrument by which the agent acts upon the object in order for the effect of the action to reach it.

f: What are the three standard patterns for اسم الآلة?
b: The standard patterns are مِفْعَل، مِفْعَلَة، مِفْعال.

f: What examples illustrate the standard patterns of اسم الآلة?
b: Examples include مِحْلَب (milking instrument), مِكْسَحَة (sweeping instrument/broom), مِفْتاح (key), and مِصْفاة (strainer/filter).

f: What is the word مِرْقاة an example of?
b: مِرْقاة (“ladder/stairway”) is given as an example formed according to the pattern of اسم الآلة.

f: What does pronouncing the mīm of مَرْقاة with fatḥah indicate?
b: If the mīm is given fatḥah, مَرْقاة, the speaker intends the place rather than the instrument.

f: Which forms of اسم الآلة are anomalous, with both the mīm and the ʿayn pronounced with ḍammah?
b: The anomalous forms are مُدْهُن، مُسْعُط، مُدُقّ، مُنْخُل، مُكْحُلَة، مُحْرُضَة.

f: What is the regular form of مِدَقّ and مِدَقّة?
b: مِدَقّ and مِدَقّة occur according to the regular pattern, with kasrah on the mīm.

f: How is the noun of a single occurrence (اسم المرة) formed from the verbal noun of a basic triliteral verb?
b: It is formed on فَعْلَة with fatḥah on the ʿayn: ضَرَبْتُ ضَرْبَةً (“I struck once”) and قُمْتُ قَوْمَةً (“I stood up once”).

f: How is the noun of a single occurrence formed from a verb with more than three radicals?
b: It is formed by adding tāʾ to the verbal noun, as in إعطاء → إعطاءَة and انطلاق → انطلاقة.

f: When is the extra tāʾ not added to form the noun of a single occurrence from an augmented verb?
b: If the verbal noun already contains tāʾ al-taʾnīth, the single occurrence is expressed by adding واحدة instead.

f: How is a single occurrence expressed when the verbal noun already contains tāʾ al-taʾnīth?
b: By saying رَحِمْتُهُ رَحْمَةً واحِدَةً (“I showed him mercy once”) and دَحْرَجْتُهُ دَحْرَجَةً واحِدَةً (“I rolled it once”).

f: What is the difference between فَعْلَة with fatḥah and فِعْلَة with kasrah?
b: فَعْلَة indicates a single occurrence of the action (اسم المرة), whereas فِعْلَة indicates the manner or type in which the action is performed (اسم الهيئة).

f: How is the noun of manner/type (اسم الهيئة) formed?
b: It is formed on فِعْلَة, with kasrah on the ʿayn.

f: What examples illustrate فِعْلَة as the noun of manner/type?
b: هُوَ حَسَنُ الطِّعْمَةِ والجِلْسَةِ: “He has a good manner of tasting/eating and a good manner of sitting.”
